recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的數個紅血球內含成簇的不規則藍紫色小顆粒（Pappenheimer bodies），其中一顆細胞質淡且顆粒散布較廣；背景其他紅血球只偶見單一小點，含鐵顆粒的紅血球即鐵粒紅血球（siderocytes）。
features: Several RBCs containing clusters of small irregular basophilic granules (arrows)
One pale red cell with more widely dispersed granules throughout the cytoplasm
Granule clusters located centrally or peripherally within affected cells
Occasional tiny single dots in other red cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows mild anisocytosis with scattered red cells containing clusters of small, irregular, basophilic granules consistent with Pappenheimer bodies (arrows); one pale erythrocyte shows more widely distributed granules. Occasional tiny dots are present in other red cells. These inclusion-bearing cells represent siderocytes, and an iron stain would confirm the ferritin/iron nature of the granules. Findings are consistent with siderocytes, as seen in hyposplenism, sideroblastic anemia, and disorders of ineffective erythropoiesis.

ddx.vs: Stippling granules are uniformly distributed throughout the cell and do not stain with Prussian blue.
Howell-Jolly bodies are single larger round dense inclusions rather than clusters of fine irregular granules.
Overlying platelets have a pale blue cytoplasmic halo around granules, whereas Pappenheimer bodies lie within the RBC without a halo.
